# Accessibility (a11y) — Flutter UI

Use these rules when building or modifying UI in `lib/**`.

## Goals

- Ensure all interactive elements are reachable (touch + keyboard) and labeled.
- Support text scaling, high contrast, and screen readers.
- Avoid regressions by validating a11y as part of normal development.

## Rules (practical)

### Semantics & labels

- Prefer Material widgets that already expose semantics.
- For custom widgets (gestures, InkWell wrappers, etc.), add explicit semantics:
  - Use `Semantics(label: ..., button: true, enabled: ...)` when appropriate.
  - Avoid empty/duplicate labels.
- For icon-only actions, always provide a `tooltip` (e.g., `IconButton(tooltip: ...)`).

### Focus order & keyboard

- Ensure focus can move through all controls (important for web/desktop).
- Use `FocusTraversalGroup` for complex forms or custom traversal.
- Don’t trap focus in dialogs/sheets; make dismiss actions discoverable.

### Text scaling & layout

- Avoid hard-coded heights that clip text.
- Prefer flexible layouts (`Expanded`, `Flexible`, wrapping) and test with large text.

### Color, contrast, and meaning

- Do not encode meaning by color alone; pair with text/icon.
- Keep interactive states distinguishable (disabled vs enabled).

### Tap targets

- Keep touch targets comfortably sized (use padding/min constraints).

## Quick verification checklist

- Screen reader: verify labels and roles make sense.
- Keyboard: tab/arrow navigation works and focus is visible.
- Layout: large text doesn’t clip or overlap.
